answer.rationale: Rollback is excluded by compliance constraint despite memory_b1's precedent, since the security patch must stay in place. The write-path latency climb over 90 minutes at peak settlement volume looks more consistent with capacity saturation (memory_b3: provisioning headroom before peak kept queue depth flat) than with a single-region failure event (memory_b2: regional failover restored latency during a discrete regional degradation). Failover during heavy write traffic risks write loss or consistency issues if the regions aren't fully write-synchronized, which conflicts with the objective of not losing customer writes, so I want to verify b2's original record to check whether that failover preserved write integrity under heavy write load before ruling it out. I also verify b3 to confirm the capacity intervention specifically addressed write-path latency (not just read/dashboard load) since b5 shows a similar-sounding fix (read replica routing) that only helped read/dashboard latency, not write latency, and I don't want to conflate those two mechanisms. Given the objective explicitly names avoiding write loss, add_capacity is the least disruptive lever that doesn't touch traffic routing or release state, so I intend to add capacity to the write path as a standard (not maximal, not merely test-scale) intervention while monitoring queue depth and p99 closely, deferring failover or breaker changes to the next window if this doesn't resolve the saturation.
